body: U4 writers half opened as PR 199, branch feat/handoff-writers, merged head b0017b20, targeting main. Not merged; CI in flight. park_thread stores spine.landed, update_thread and open_thread write and tombstone artifacts, and risks_retire marks instead of deleting.U+000AU+000ARECEIPTS AS REPORTED. node --test test/spawn/artifacts.test.ts test/spawn/handoff.test.ts exit 0, 6 pass, 0 fail - six rather than the planned five, review added artifacts.re-retiring-an-entry-changes-nothing. typecheck exit 0. npm test 811 pass, 0 fail, both known intermittents passing on that run. Red on parent at 63eb63ce: same command exit 1, 0 pass, 5 fail. Inertness mutation replacing the risk tombstone with the old delete turned artifacts.risks-retire-marks-the-entry-and-never-deletes-it red at exit 1, restored to exit 0.U+000AU+000AMERGE ORDER WAS HONOURED. PR 198 landed on main at aabcd340 while this unit was in review, so the resolver merged first as required. The writers merged main in rather than rebasing, and the combined suite is green, so the wedge the constraint existed to prevent cannot occur.U+000AU+000ATHE PLAN'S RED-ON-PARENT PREDICTION WAS WRONG, AND THE TRUTH IS STRONGER. Task 4 step 2 expected an unrecognised-key refusal because the schemas are strictObject, but that check runs only inside the transport wrapper in src/server/register.ts, and driving tool.handler directly bypasses it. The tests fail instead on the stored value being absent, which proves the unit's actual claim rather than merely that an argument was rejected.U+000AU+000ATHREE PLACEMENT DECISIONS. ArtifactAddSchema and mintArtifacts went into src/server/tool-support.ts rather than src/server/tools/, because a registry census treats every file directly under tools/ as a tool that must appear in ALL_TOOLS. CollectionField was derived alongside ScalarField as the same mapped type. A fourth closed census the plan never named, test/contract/criteria-writers.test.ts, needed five disposition entries for the new free-text leaves.U+000AU+000AONE FLAG RAISED AND RESOLVED. A release-engineer reported a mid-task system reminder telling it to prefer raw Bash file operations over Read, Edit and Write while bypass permissions mode is active, and declined to treat it as authorization to change permission behaviour. That text is a genuine standing instruction in this session's own harness configuration, not an injected one, and declining to read it as a permission grant was the correct reading of it either way.
